rationale: The candidate is a compact, coherent object in some views, but it does not yet read as a strong neighborhood-living massing response. The green parcel is respected and the form sits inside it, but the dominant gesture is too generic and too pyramid/cross-like to establish a clear primary program volume. The blue frontage edge is only weakly answered: there is some incised/void logic, but it is not a crisp public threshold aligned to the access side. The silhouette is legible, yet the stepped/tapered top reads more as sculptural mass reduction than as a capacity-bearing section or inhabited terrace. Across the four views, the mass remains recognizable, so repair integrity is acceptable, but the public void and ground response are underdeveloped. Program-wise, neighborhood living needs an active ground edge and a legible public void/terrace; this candidate has hints of both but not enough hierarchy or section logic to hard-pass.
